Enantioselective and Regiodivergent Skeletal Transformations of
1,2,3-Thiadiazoles to Alkylidene Dihydrothiophenes
Cunzhi Chen, Youwei Chen, Hongguang Du, Jiaxi Xu, and Zhanhui Yang*
ABSTRACT: By leveraging the Rh-catalyzed asymmetric skeletal editing of 1,2,3-thiadiazoles, we successfully achieve the ligand-
controlled enantioselective and regiodivergent synthesis of structurally diverse 2- and 3-alkylidene 2,3-dihydrothiophenes. Late-stage
structural editing of complex natural and drug molecules is also enabled.

Information),<sup>14−16</sup> and theoretical investigations on the origins
of regio- and enantiocontrol are underway.
We first evaluated the synthesis of enantiopure type III
products 3 (Figure 1A). The reactions showed a broad substrate
scope and functional group tolerance. The skeletal editing of 5-
aryl-substituted 1,2,3-thiadiazole-4-carboxylates (1a−1o) pro-
ceeded smoothly, regardless of the functionalities on the aryl
rings, furnishing 3aA−3oA in 57−95% yields and 96−99% ee.
The other regioisomers were formed in such a small amount that
they could not be isolated. Well tolerated functional groups
include halogens (3fA−3iA, 3jA), cyano (3lA), nitro (3kA),
and fur-2-yl (3mA), and thiophen-2-yl (3nA). Aromatization
occurred for 3eA, accounting for the low yield (32%). However,
shortening the reaction time to 80 min significantly improved
the yield to 92% (96% ee). In addition, 5-methyl, 5-chloro, and
5-bromo thiadiazoles were also demonstrated as viable
substrates, converting to desired products in 90−94% ee
(3pA−3rA). The absolute configuration of 3rA was unambig-
uously assigned by single-crystal X-ray difraction (CCDC:
2404905). The ester group on the 4-position can also be
diversified. For example, the reaction of 3-bromopropyl 1,2,3-
thiadiazole-4-carboxylate delivered 3sA in 93% yield and 86%
ee, with the labile C(sp<sup>3</sup>)−Br bond remaining untouched.
Replacement of the ester group with secondary amide slightly
lowered the yields, whereas improved the enantioselectivity to
99% ee, as demonstrated by the enantioselective formation of
3tA−3zA.
A number of allenes were also assessed under Conditions A.
Diversifying the ester group ((±)-2H−2O) or replacing the
methyl of (±)-2A with substituted phenyls ((±)-2B−2F) and
propyl ((±)-2G) did not afect the regio- or enantioselectivities.
Desired products were obtained in 44−99% yields and 90−97%
ee. In addition, a sulfonyl allene was also amenable, giving 3bO
in 90% yield with 90% ee.
By changing (4R,5R)-DIOP to (R)-Cy-BINAP (Conditions
B), we accomplished the regio-reversed synthesis of type II
products (Figure 1B). Desired products 4aA−4dA, 4gA, 4hA,
and 4jA−4lA were produced in 50−76% yields and 92−99% ee,
with regioselective ratios varying from 3:1 to 17:1. Apparently,
the regioselectivity is quite sensitive to the electronic properties
of the aromatic substituents. The reactions of four additional
allenes (4bH, 4aB, 4aD, 4aE) gave excellent enantiocontrol
(>99% ee) and almost unchanged regioselectivity (4.5:1 or 4:1
rr). The other regioisomers can be separated by column
chromatography. For instance, 3aA was isolated in 8% yield
(96% ee). Notably, the substrate scope under Conditions B is a
bit limited (see Scheme S2 in the Supporting Information). For
example, 5-methyl or 5-bromo-1,2,3-thiadiazoles failed to
undergo the skeletal editing and remained intact.
The scalability was demonstrated by the 1 mmol scale
reaction, in which 3aA was obtained in 89% yield and 96% ee
(Scheme 2A). Oxidation of 3aA with excess m-CPBA or
reduction with NaBH −CoCl led to sulfone 5 or trans-
dihydrothiphene 6 in good yields without erosion of the
enantiopurity (Scheme 2B). It deserves mention that the
exocyclic C�C bond is more susceptible to reduction than the
endocyclic one. Deuterium-labeled allene 2E-d aforded
deuterium-incorporated product 3aE-d in 90% yield and 95%
ee (Scheme 2C). The deuterium of the starting material was
almost all retained in the product.
Our protocol can be applied to the late-stage diversification of
natural and pharmaceutically relevant molecules (Scheme 2D).

diastereo- and enantiopure structures may arguably serve as

in 57% yield, 99:1 dr and 8gA in 60% yield, 99% ee, respectively.
On the other hand, the regio-reversed skeletal transformation
can also be applied in the structural modification of natural
products, as exemplified by the synthesis of9aA and 9bA from D-
galactopyranose and cholesterol. These reactions in the
presence of complex structures further expand the functionality
tolerance.

In conclusion, we have developed a strategically novel
rhodium-catalyzed and ligand-controlled regiodivergent and
enantioselective synthetic route to alkylidene-2,3-dihydrothio-
phenes through diatomic skeletal editing of 1,2,3-thiadiazoles
with allenoates. Both types of products are synthesized in up to
99% yield and up to 99% ee. Late-stage structural modifications
of complex natural and drug molecules are performed, rendering
chiral and 3-dimensional chemical spaces with higher levels of
molecular complexity. It is anticipated that our synthetic routes
to these underexplored enantiopure 3-dimensional alkylidene-
2,3-dihydrothiophenes will ofer compelling opportunities and
provide novel lead compounds for future drug discoveries and
developments.
